fix: the sync checksum covers what decides a unit's next move; DDS sizes checked before allocating (#395)

* fix: a DDS alpha mask is made only once its payload is known to be there

Review finding: AlphaMask::from_dds allocated its mask from the header's
declared size before checking the file held that much data; a 128-byte
file declaring 65536 x 65536 asked for 512 MiB before it was refused.
The format and the payload it needs are worked out first, in 64-bit
sizes, and a file that holds less is refused before any allocation; a
side past 16384 (FA's UI textures are at most 2048) gives no mask.

Tests: truncated and oversized files of each format, malformed headers,
the exact payload accepted, the decoders' texels; and, in a child whose
address space allows 64 MiB more than it has, the review's file refused
without an allocation failure (it failed so before the fix).


* sim: the sync checksum covers the state that decides what a unit does next

Review finding: the snapshot serializers keep state that
SimState::checksum_parts didn't read, so two states could share a
checksum while differing in what decides their next move. A ground
attack's shot count, for one, decides when its order goes round the
queue.

Added, each in its domain (blocks mixed only while set, as the
existing ones are):
- weapons: a ground attack's order, shots and last point; the
  target-check clock; what scripts change (range, rate of fire,
  damage, damage radius, target layers);
- units: the hull's facing work (slaved turn, attack facing, turn in
  place); statistics (KILLS...) and named states, sorted by name;
  script flags off their defaults (busy, blocked queue, damage and
  kill immunity, crashing, teleporting, jostled); speed, acceleration
  and turn multipliers; veterancy, last attacker, enhancements;
  collision detectors' watched bones;
- orders: an attack's facing clock;
- navigation: heading and elevation target;
- armies: platoons (id, unique name, DisbandOnIdle, units).

Tests: each of these, set off its default, changes the checksum (each
fails without this change); a game saved with them set, restored and
played on 30 ticks matches the one that went on. The cross-platform
synthetic game's pinned checksum is updated on purpose (0x01950e69).


* fix: a DDS's mip sizes are checked in 64 bits against the bytes it holds

parse_dds sized each mip level in u32. A 65536 x 65536 DXT5 level is
4 GiB of blocks, which wrapped to 0, and a 0-byte level passed the
truncation check: a 144-byte file parsed as a 65536-square texture, and
dds_to_rgba then sized a 16 GiB image from it and read blocks past the
file. A width at the top of u32 wrapped its block count the same way.

Sizes are now 64-bit and checked against what is left of the file, sides
past 16384 are refused (D3D9 gives Moho nothing wider on any card it
runs on), and the header's mip count is clamped to a full chain before
the level list is reserved: 0xFFFFFFFF levels asked for ~100 GB there.
dds_to_rgba checks a BC3 level holds its blocks before decoding it.

None of retail's 14,276 DDS files is affected: the widest side is 2048
and no mip count runs past its chain.


* test: every new checksum field changes it on its own, and survives a save

Review found the coverage test left some of the newly mixed fields
untouched: a weapon's MinRadius and DamageRadius, the acceleration and
turn multipliers and the jostled flag were never changed alone, and the
save-and-restore case saved most fields at their defaults, so it proved
nothing of their serializers. Each now gets a row, and the saved game
carries them off their defaults (a weapon's script-set parameters and
target clock, the unit's flags, multipliers, heading, elevation target,
last attacker, and a queued attack's facing clock).

Crashing and teleporting stay unrowed: only a death in flight or a
teleport order sets them, and both change other mixed state with them.


* docs: the checksum's coverage of what happens next, and the test count

Fixed in the integration for its own linux-asan failure (arch.status_metrics: docs/current-state.md says 1,060 unit test cases, the ASan build has 1,059): the new test that refuses a huge truncated DDS under an address-space limit was compiled out under ASan, so ASan builds listed one test case fewer. It is now always registered on Linux and SKIPs under ASan. tests/CMakeLists.txt gives catch_discover_tests SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4, so ctest reports a skipped test as skipped: Catch2 exits 4 when the one test it runs skips.

commit.message:
Hash the executable once per open (#160)

* Hash the executable once per open

Each static query read and SHA-256 hashed the whole executable, about
1.2 s per call on M452. Installation::open now keeps the hashed bytes
and the file's metadata stamp: length and modification time, and on
Unix device, inode and status-change time. A later query reads and
hashes the file again only when the stamp differs, so a changed
executable still gives TargetChanged with the same sticky invalidation.
performance.md states the accepted limit: a byte change that keeps the
stamp is not detected between queries.

Recording all 2,178 M452 command grammars now takes 170 s, not about
43 minutes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Hash every byte before a game starts

Installation::target_integrity, which start_game and the supervisor's
checks before spawn use, reads and hashes the whole executable again
whatever the metadata stamp says. A game started from a changed
executable would use the layouts of another build, and the hash costs
about one second against a launch of 16-21 s. Static reads keep the
stamp check.

Tell a Locate view apart by its name when Lich rewrites the roomName (#248)

## Problem
#247 sends a view of another room (DR's Locate) to the familiar window
when the roomName's game id differs from the last `<nav rm>`. In play it
didn't fire for Fidon (`DR-Fidon/2026/10/2026-10-07_13-38-12.xml`): the
room window still showed the located room.

Fidon's Lich settings are `display_uid=true`, `display_lichid=true` and
`display_roomid_location=title`. With them, Lich's
`DragonRealms#modify_room_display` (lich-5 `games.rb`) rewrites every
roomName before the front-end gets it. It drops the game's `] (NNN)` and
appends ` - <Lich id> - (u<uid>)` inside the brackets. The ids come from
`Map.current` and `XMLData.room_id`, which describe the room the player
is in, whatever room the line names. So the Locate view reached
Profanity as `[Bosque Deriel, Hermit's Shacks - <id> - (u230007)]`. It
had no game id, and the only id left was the player's own. The `.xml`
logs record the stream before Lich's rewrite, which is why replaying the
raw log through #247 works.

The room subtitle isn't rewritten for Profanity: Lich rebuilds the
subtitle only for front-ends with the `room_window` capability, and
Profanity's definition has `xml` and `streams`.

## Change
- `RoomAssembler#remote_title?`:
- When the roomName has the game's id and a nav tag with an id has been
seen, the ids decide, as in #247.
- Otherwise the names decide: the view is another room's when its name
isn't the last subtitle's (`@subtitle_name`, set in `#subtitle`).
- `#same_room_name?` accepts the subtitle's name either alone or
followed by ` - `, which is what Lich's `;display roomid title` appends
inside the brackets.
- A view counts as remote only in a session that has sent a nav tag, and
only in a burst with no nav tag (`@nav_in_burst`, reset when a prompt's
line ends) and no room subtitle. Both games send a nav tag with every
room change, so in such a session an inline view without one is a LOOK
or another room's view, not a move. Without nav tags, a move that
arrives without components (`room_description_spec.rb`, "drops the old
room's description for a room that arrives without components") can't be
told from a view, so it stays the player's room.
- USER_GUIDE §3.6 is updated.

## Tests
- `spec/lib/room_remote_view_spec.rb` adds Fidon's 13:38 log
(`spec/fixtures/room_pipeline/dr_locate_after_move.xml`, minus
`dialogData` and `exp` component lines): north to the Hermit's Shacks,
south to the Burial Ground, then a Locate of a character in the Hermit's
Shacks. It replays the log with Lich's rewrite applied as
`modify_room_display` does under those settings; the Lich ids in the
spec are made up. The room window keeps the Burial Ground, and the
familiar window gets the view. It also covers:
  - a Lich-rewritten LOOK in the player's room;
  - a view without the game's id, told apart by name;
- a view of a room with the player's room's name, which stays the
player's room;
- a move that sends a nav tag but no subtitle, which stays the player's
room;
  - a view before any nav tag or subtitle.
- Fail-first: on main b58766c, the Lich-rewrite example and the name
example fail. #247's "takes a view without the game's room id as the
player's room" became "tells a view without the game's room id apart by
its name".
- Suite: 3,602 examples, 0 failures. RuboCop: no offenses on the changed
files. `yard doc --private --fail-on-warning` exits 0, and
`script/check_yard_tags.rb` finds 0 gaps.

Not covered:
- What Profanity receives is reconstructed from the Lich code running on
the host (`games.rb` at staging b981e803), not captured, because
Profanity has no raw-input log.
- A Locate into a room with the same name as the player's, and a Locate
before the first move since Profanity started (no nav tag or subtitle
seen yet), still fill the room window.

zrcp-verify: the MAME harness can time

The 128K was felt to walk slower than the Next, and nothing in the harness
could say by how much, or where the time went, without distorting it:
ZRCP pauses the CPU on every read. MAME can, and mame.lua now does:

- sampleon [hz] / sampleoff <label>: PC sampled on emu.wait timers, at
  exact emulated instants, with the 128K's paged bank read from BANKM;
  a histogram per label.
- hold <key> <frames> / release: a matrix key held down -- the held walk.
- watch <addr> <n>: bytes logged with their emulated time whenever they
  change (hero_x, hero_y, turns; on the 128K, draw_map's prev_hx gives
  each move's time to the frame that drew it).
- copy <src> <dst> <n>: bytes copied at run time, so a fixed script can
  act on what the game decided (put the hero on @dn_x/@dn_y).
- Get-MameNewGame -Seed: the title seeds the world from how long its key
  took, so two builds whose tapes load in different times played
  different worlds. Poking world_seed and the play RNG while the class
  picker waits, before any level exists, gives every build the same one.
- mameprof.py turns a log into a profile of the turn's work (key polling
  and the ROM's IM1 handler left out) and the step timing: each hold's
  step periods, each move's time until it was drawn.

SKILL.md has the recipe, and a trap found on the way: two MAME runs cannot
share one .tap -- MAME opens it read-write and the second dies on
"Permission denied", without a log.

Season 2, Cold Snap, follows Space Race with no gap: Jan 5 to Mar 8, 2027, a free pass of 30 levels and a Pass+ row with five bonus levels, as Ramsey wants seasons back to back so there's always a pass and a Pass+ to buy into. He picked its look, A · Northern Lights, from three on the Seasons canvas ("Season 2 · Cold Snap, three looks"): a polar night, aurora green where Space Race had orange, teal and violet beside it, Russo One lettering.

What it gives (the API's seasons.ts has the levels):
- Free row: the Season 2 patch (pin s2), five titles (Cold Snap, Snow Day, Hot Cocoa, First Frost, Snow Bunny), three name styles (Frost, Frostbite, Glacier), four badge finishes (Snowflake, Igloo, Snowman, Blizzard), three card themes (Snowfield, Ski lodge, Pine forest), two confetti (Snowfall, Snowballs), the Cold Snap wall sign, and a skin for each skin game: Ice Breaker (Lander), Icicle (Asteroids), Snowbird (Barrage), Ice rocket (Hot Lap) and Snowdrift tail (Snake).
- Pass+: ten skins (Ice crystal, Gondola, Whiteout, Snowy owl, North Star, Aurora tail, Borealis, Fireside tail, Frost dragon, Yeti) and fifteen looks (Snow Angel, Ice Cold, Polar Explorer and Cold Snap Legend titles; Hoarfrost, Polar and Crystal name styles; Frozen lake, Ice cave and Northern lights cards; Icicles and Flurry confetti; Polar bear, Diamond dust and Ice crown finishes). Its stage's headliners are Frost dragon, Borealis and Yeti.
- The goal of keeping the Dailies on 30 days gives the Snowbound title.

Its look:
- season.css: Space Race's colours are tokens now, and .season-cold-snap gives them Cold Snap's values. The dressing (SeasonDressing) draws snow-light stars and the northern lights where the planet was, and its Spotlight flag is a snowflake.
- SeasonLook.tsx picks the live season's patch and banner scene (ColdSnapArt.tsx: FrostPatch, AuroraScene: the Ice Breaker over a frozen lake under the lights). The header's ring, the rails and the home banner take the accent from the tokens. The Season page carries its season's class and lettering.
- Skins are drawn in skinArt.ts as the others are. A skin's `burn` gives its engine flame its picture's colours (teal, green or violet) in Asteroids and Barrage; Season 1's keep their orange. Lander's follows once another session's Lander work in scene.ts is in. Hot Lap's are two Rocket colour sets with icy wheel rims (`rim`, new; Season 1's cars keep orange) and Whiteout, an Indy livery, each rendered from the 3D car into assets/season. Challenge cards' pictures came from `npm run icons:skins`.
- The finishes, name styles, card themes, confetti and sign are in their own files beside Season 1's (WinterFinishes, WinterNames, WinterCardThemes, winterConfetti, WinterRewardArt).

The handover: lib/season.ts asks /season again the moment the live season ends (or the next starts), and a season whose last day is over isn't treated as live, so a page left open moves from Space Race to Cold Snap at midnight New York time without a reload. The Season page's title follows the date (lib/seasonCalendar.ts). /admin's Season card can preview a chosen season ("Preview Cold Snap"), so Cold Snap can be tried on staging while Space Race runs. The API side is in ramseys-arcade-api.

BladeBall: tighten the parry-capture hooks around the game's real sender

Read the game's parry sender (the PRY module under SwordsController). It sends
the real parry either as remote:FireServer or by fetching FireServer first (both
hooks stay), can fire a decoy 8-argument packet at another remote before the real
one, and runs two client checks per parry: debug.info must still be native, and
no caller up to 10 levels may have an executor environment. The capture hooks
don't trip either (debug.info is only called, and the hooks run below the sender,
not above it), so this tightens them:

- Decoy-proof: every match in one send is noted and the last full packet (the
  real one) is kept once the send finishes, instead of relying on ordering.
- Shape check on the raw arguments first (8+ args, CFrame 5th), so every other
  FireServer passes straight through with nothing copied.
- Capture runs under pcall inside the hooks, so nothing of ours can error into
  the game's own parry.
- Arm window cut from 1.2s to 0.6s; the sender runs within a frame of the press.
